notes.title: Ho ho ho! A gift for y'all!
notes.content:
After a long time in the dark, we're "cooking" (pun intended) something that you might like.

Meanwhile, got something for you: many bugfixes and especially a massive change to the renderer, so now even the absolute worst laptop could run the game. Ok, maybe not the worst, as this isn't Doom 1993, but still, you should see and experience massive performance improvements.

Changelog:

Most importantly: redid the renderer so it should work even on potato PCs.

Changes:


 Showing patience over customers
 Improvements to Uniform Editor
 Improvements to Group Uniforms
 Added information as to why Employees seem to be idling
 Added fail-safes to Drinks when Food needs to be made
 Improved rain dance so it doesn't rain for several days in a row
 Bathrooms no longer flood the entire Restaurant
 Improvements to Main Menu announcements
 Relaxed rats so they don't cause so many issues, so often
 Improved panels functionality to avoid blur effects
 Improved Objectives Panel so they scale properly in all resolutions, in all languages
 Improved and added Events
 Improved and added Paintings
 Improved Mood indicator for Employees
 Improved camera controls
 Improved flavour for some ingredients (no longer "gross")
 Improved Popularity counter
 Fire is now less aggressive
 Increased max Employee count


Fixes:


 Fixed tutorial steps relative to customers
 Fixed employees loving and hating the same thing
 Avoiding the chance for multiple critics to be in the restaurant at the same time
 Bar chairs reserved too often
 People complaining about the Bar when there isn't one
 Employees no longer complain about the rain when it's not raining
 Removed object cloning exploit
 Improved Customer eyesight so that they can easily find beloved items on the menu
 Redone shadow renderer to avoid black screens on some GPUs
 New Employees now actually show up for work
 Cannot move stuff on fire anymore
 Cannot save-scum dialogue anymore
 Free food is now free

notes.title: Update 0.7 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I’m excited to announce our latest update is now live! This time, the team has been focusing on using feedback from the community to refine our existing mechanics and improve the overall gameplay experience. We’ve added a couple of new features to the game, too! Check out our Dev Update video below to get a closer look at some of the changes we’ve made.

[previewyoutube=4CFy8SulItc;full][/previewyoutube]

Updated Character Models 
Employees and customers have been revamped and updated to boost the game visuals up to the next level! 

New Customer Types
Players will now see a wide range of groups coming through their restaurant doors. Not only will these groups share visual similarities, but they’ll have common traits and food preferences, too!

Mood Mechanics
Customer patience and Employee stress will now be called ‘mood’. Mood increases as a result of positive thoughts and decreases with negative ones. Don’t forget to check the thoughts recap to better understand your customers and employees!

Special Recipe Tags
Combining specific ingredients and cooking actions will now apply a ‘special tag’ to a recipe. Based on things like cuisine and healthiness, players will have to experiment with their recipes in order to discover these additional tags.

New Traits
There are 18 new traits for you to explore! From ‘Flatulent’ and ‘Stone Cold’, to ‘Big Bladder’ and ‘Chatty’, it’s up to you to discover what effects these new traits will have on restaurant life.

Revised Tutorial & QOL Updates
We’ve updated the tutorial and added advisory notifications, so you’ll have all the info you need to be on your way. We’ve also made some overall UI improvements that will streamline certain gameplay aspects.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/a1005eb22008726a0ab7f3c800307e1b25225526.png

As always, we’d love to hear your feedback! Feel free to stop by our Twitter and Discord channels to share your thoughts, screenshots and recipes.

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer – Dapper Penguin Studios.

We’ve put together an update video detailing all of the new content for you to take a look at, enjoy!

[previewyoutube=aMPacQNEsIU;full][/previewyoutube]

As always we’d love to hear what you think about the new content and systems, so feel free to drop by our Twitter and Discord channels. If you’ve got the time you can also have your say on specific gameplay elements, and which roadmap development items we should be working on next by completing the in-game feedback form. It’s greatly appreciated!

I’ll be back with another update outlining what we’ll be working on next in the coming weeks, so speak soon!

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios.

notes.title: Developer Update #9 - A taste of what’s to come...
notes.content:
Hi everyone, before we take a break for the holiday season I wanted to check in and give you a quick update of what we’re currently working on for Recipe for Disaster’s next major Early Access update, which is scheduled to arrive in January 2022. 

Following the release of the Freeplay & Festive updates we’ve been reviewing all of the feedback that you’ve submitted to date. A recurring theme amongst the community has been that you would like to see more content generally, and that the Expanded Campaign EA milestone has consistently ranked high as one of the most requested features since launch. 

With this in mind, we’ll be basing our next update around improving and expanding the campaign, adding additional content to the existing stages and introducing more levels which showcase some entirely new gameplay mechanics!

Expanded campaign update - What to expect

More disasters - We’re currently working on two new disasters, one of which involves a sudden influx of pesky rodents, while the other will be tied to ‘unforeseen plumbing issues’ within your restrooms. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/69c6d12b46bbc646fb4f37b871482bc406b0f59b.png
(Work in progress)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/dfde6cf7fe45ad3503804d5c254df627e96369dc.png
(Work in progress)

Additional dynamic events - Each level will gain some additional dynamic events with some being unique to the stage’s story and setting.

VIPs - Upon arrival, these influential customer types will trigger a new kind of event which will involve having to exceed their incredibly high expectations, or face the wrath of their follower base or readership!    

Health inspections - A fledgling restaurant’s worst nightmare… Health inspectors will occasionally visit your establishment and grade both it’s overall cleanliness, and the quality of its food.   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/ceef99185347444b5e5cebbefe23d404f5a24b41.png
(Work in progress)

We can’t wait to share more progress with you in January, but until then have a great Christmas and a Happy New Year!

Alex Mochi 
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Developer Update #8 - Festive update!
notes.content:
It’s beginning to feel a lot like Christmas, and to get you all in the festive mood we’ve added some fun new holiday themed content to Freeplay mode! 

We’ve also teamed up with the fine folks at The Yogscast for their annual Jingle Jam event! You can catch Ravs and Sips playing Recipe for Disaster for the first time LIVE on 3rd December during their morning Twitch stream between 11am-2pm GMT (with catch up on their YouTube channel). 

Now, let’s take a look at what’s in store for you with this latest update: 

Festive decorative objects

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/85640b7d3f2e6109152798476f613021380155f4.jpg

Christmas tree - Spruce up your restaurant with this attractive tree, complete with decorations, lights, presents, and golden star!

Christmas wreath -  Add a tasteful yuletide wreath decoration to your dining area, baubles and bright red bow included. 

Christmas lights - Brighten up your customer’s moods with multicoloured fairy lights which can be strung together for that ultimate festive feel.  

Log fire and chimney - Build a cozy hearth and smoking chimney, along with Christmas stockings and a selection of colourful christmas cards! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/d7ddb4134fc5f5e23007dfdcee478eb7c2b83b03.jpg

Festive avatar & uniform editor items

Santa uniform - Kit out your chef and staff with these Christmas themed uniform items including two-tone santa hat, coat, and trousers. You can even customize the colours!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/34adb1c6f0e8314c3657e424d44d668860147ebd.png

Snowy weather  

The weather will occasionally change to bring forth a mighty blizzard! Be careful as customers caught waiting out in the snow will be far more impatient to get a seat...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/8b641de789d92ef51fd870cf6d5dd97b5f8e11e9.jpg

Remember, if you have any comments and ideas about future content, or if you want to share a screenshot of your festive creations, you can post on the Steam forums, Twitter or Discord.

On a side note, since launch we’ve received loads of feedback and words of encouragement from the community, so if you are enjoying the game, we’d really appreciate it if you’d also consider leaving us a review on Steam. We’re a small team, so any extra support that you can give us at this stage is truly appreciated!

Rest assured, I’ll be back with another update soon, but until then wishing you all a very Merry Christmas from all of us here at the studio!

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios.

notes.title: Developer Update #7 - Freeplay mode is live!
notes.content:
Hey everyone, in our last post we looked at your feedback following the first week of release. Taking on board what the community asked for, we’ve been hard at work on creating a highly customizable Freeplay mode, which is now live for you all to play and enjoy! This is the first iteration of Freeplay and we’ll continue to develop it alongside other existing systems and mechanics as we move through early access. 

In this post I’ll be giving you a full breakdown of all the new features and options that come with Recipe for Disaster’s first EA update. 

Difficulty presets

First of all, we wanted to make it really easy for players to jump straight into a new game, so when you first select Freeplay mode you will have the following options to choose from:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/eb2a392e0307f57da43e5aac088c1c08423d0b6b.png

Easy - You’ll have lots of starting money, decent starting popularity, and many employees to choose from each day. There will be no losing conditions. Dirt will accumulate slowly, fire probability will be low, and employee stress will be easy to manage!

Medium - Starting money and popularity will be average, and you’ll have less prospective employees each day. You’ll lose if you have a negative balance at the end of the day or if an employee is fired or quits. Dirt and employee stress will accumulate faster, and fires will be more frequent. This is the default Campaign difficulty.

Hard - Prepare for a real challenge. Starting money and popularity will be low, and you’ll have very few employees to choose from. You’ll lose if you have a negative balance at any time or if just one employee hits a breakpoint! Customer flow and variety will be high, and they’ll be much less patient and way less willing to pay high prices. They’ll also be far more critical with their review scores. You’ll see dirt and employee stress accumulate faster, and fires will be an ever present threat...         

Custom - Now this is where things get interesting, here you’ll be able to customize your own game down to the finest detail.    

Freeplay - Custom settings

Naturally many of you will want to be able to configure your experience, so we’ve made it possible for you to be able to tweak almost everything in the game. You can also share your settings with other players as each configuration will generate its own seed. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/f937a8c0a800c8a68c292db088dd2065d085922c.png

General settings 

Starting money - How much money you start with. You can also toggle infinite money on/off.

Starting popularity - Your restaurant’s starting popularity.

Location - Select whether your restaurant will be located in the residential area, suburbs, projects, or downtown. 

Losing conditions - Select your losing conditions for the game:

 Negative balance at end of day (Medium)
 An employee is fired or quits (Medium)
 Negative balance at any time (Hard)
 Hit any employee breakpoint (Hard)

PLEASE NOTE: We’re planning on adding more of these at a later date.

Dynamic events - Toggle customer and employee dynamic events on/off.

World events - Toggle world events such as ingredient discounts or customer rush on/off.

Dining room settings 

Theme - Pick your customer’s food preferences from seafood, steak house, fast-food, homely, or none.

Customer variety - Decide how differentiated your customer’s food preferences will be within the chosen theme.

Customer flow - Configure the number of customers that will come to your restaurant. 

Patience rate - Choose how quickly your customers will run out of patience. 

Restrooms - Decide how frequently your customers will use the restroom.

Dirtiness - Select the speed in which dirt accumulates within the restaurant. 

Reviews - Define how lenient or harsh your customers will be with their review ratings. 

Kitchen settings 

Starting employees - Pick how many prospective employees will be available on day 1. 

Employees for hire - Configure how many employees will be available to hire each day. 

Employee salaries - Decide how high or low your employee’s salaries will be. 

Stress rate - Set the difficulty for managing employee stress levels. 

Fires - Set the frequency of fire disasters. 

Fair dishes markup % - Choose how much your customers will be willing to pay for their food. 

Infinite ingredients - Toggle infinite ingredients on/off. 

Objectives & Trophies   

We’ve designed Recipe for Disaster’s Freeplay mode so the player experience can range from calm and relaxing (for those of you who just want to build), to intense and stressful (for those that would prefer a challenge). While there are no ‘required’ objectives to hit, we thought it would be fun to include some optional objectives to work towards beating. Of course you can choose to ignore these but if you do decide to have a go at them you’ll unlock trophies which are placeable objects that give your restaurant a huge ambiance boost!  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/43ee842f307b445a1fd153f3a272b6caab23b87c.jpg

Each trophy tier is linked to three objectives which relate to core aspects of restaurant management:

Food profits: Make € X from selling food. 
5 star reviews: Gain X 5 star customer reviews. 
Seated tables: Have X seated tables at any one time.

...and at each tier you can unlock: 

Tier 1 trophy - Foodies review
Tier 2 trophy - TripInstructor’s Award
Tier 3 trophy - ‘The Dish’
Tier 4 trophy - Tasty Cup
Tier 5 trophy - Golden Chef Statue

Getting all of these trophies will be no easy task, and we’d love to see screenshots of your award-winning restaurants on Twitter and Discord. 

Thanks to your suggestions, we've also added 25 new ingredients to Freeplay mode (we'll add these to the campaign as it expands further).

That’s all for now but we’ve got some festive treats lined up in December so we’ll be back with another update very soon!

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Developer Update #6 - Release week & your feedback
notes.content:
Hi everyone! I’d like to start things off by saying a huge thank you to everyone who has supported Recipe for Disaster at this first stage of early access! 

While your enthusiasm and words of encouragement have been fantastic to see, we’ve also really appreciated the amount of detailed and constructive feedback that the growing community has submitted so far. Even after just 1 week it’s given us a great indication of what we need to be prioritising along the development roadmap. 

I thought it would be a good idea to share with you some of the most commonly requested feedback items, as well as our immediate plans so you can have a clearer understanding of the next steps we’re taking to make the game a more enjoyable experience for everyone. 

Your feedback

Via the in-game feedback form we’ve been asking you what your top 3 most anticipated roadmap updates are, and the results are in:  

[olist]
 Freeplay mode
 Bar area
 Expanded campaign
[/olist]
Alongside the in-game form we’ve also been monitoring the the #suggestions-box channel on our Discord, steam reviews, steam forum, and Twitter to gather your thoughts and feedback on existing mechanics and systems. The top 3 most discussed areas are: 
[olist]
 Recipe editor + customer reviews system (linked)
 Restaurant building & customization options
 Cleaning & fire disaster + employee welfare (linked)
[/olist]
We’re reading through all the comments related to these areas at the moment and are working on a plan to address some of the highest frequency items and issues. 

Update 1 - Freeplay mode

The most requested feature by far has been the addition of a freeplay mode, and so this is our current development focus for update 1. This new gameplay mode will feature:

Configurable starting conditions - Starting money, lose conditions, events frequency, plot size, disaster frequency and lots more!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/9a4cb9db3d557dc6b1e946c2175e9f165c2b8364.jpg
(Work in progress screenshot)

Difficulty presets (Easy, medium, hard, custom) - To make it easier to jump straight into a new game, or load your custom settings. 

A 5 tier milestone system - 15 milestones to work towards completing during each gameplay session. The achievements are divided into sets of 3 across 5 tiers so you can slowly work towards beating them all (and only if you want to!). You may even unlock some special items as a reward! 

We’re also working on toning down the frequency of fire disasters and how these affect employee stress levels, and we’ll be rolling out a rebalancing patch to address this shortly. 

For update 1 we’ll aim to have this live on 23rd November.   

I’m hoping you’re as excited as we are to start exploring more of what Recipe for Disaster has to offer in the coming weeks!

I’ll be back soon with another update, 

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster Developer Update #5
notes.content:
Hey everyone, I hope you’re all good! It’s been a little while since our last update but I’m happy to say we’ve got plenty of new information heading your way. Today I’m going to be talking about updates to our EA roadmap, the game’s release date, as well as progress on a number of new features that we’ve added since our last post.  

EA roadmap changes & release update

I’d like to start off by talking about an important decision we’ve made to implement a number of key features at launch that were originally planned as updates for early access. Ultimately we want players to have the very best possible experience from day 1, so Recipe for Disaster will now include the following at release:

Mini campaign
Take on a variety of challenges in a multistage narrative driven campaign.

Upgradeable appliances 
Equip your kitchen with appliances that range from basic to professional and affect dish quality.  

Restrooms 
Add facilities and objects for the comfort and convenience of your customers and staff.

Cleaning
Staff must keep on top of cleaning floors, surfaces, and appliances to maintain high review scores.

Fire Disasters
Contend with the first major disaster, restaurant fires! 

If you caught our last update video you’ll know that we’ve already added employee skill progression and perks, dynamic events, changes to how recruitment works, a uniform editor and grouping tool, localisation, and initial steam workshop support. 

We’re also currently refining the staff welfare system and how breaking points work, but we’ll come back to that in our next post. 

So the new updated EA roadmap currently looks like this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/ce4fe3856ca432ec3d15744108351042343e3459.jpg

Note that during early access we plan to expand the campaign, and add more dynamic events and disasters!. 

Unfortunately this additional content will take time to implement which means that we have had to make the difficult call to push release back to Q4 2021 (the exact date will be announced in a few weeks time). We appreciate that this will be disappointing news for some of you but hope that you’ll understand our reasoning.

Changes to table placement

We’ve recently been working hard on improving the system for placing tables in build mode. Those of you that played our demo will know that previously tables and chairs needed to have  
all surrounding tiles clear in order to be placed. This restriction created problems when building walls before placing objects and meant that large areas of the restaurant’s dining areas were not being utilised efficiently. 

With the new system we’ve amended these placement rules so that you can now freely build tables and chairs anywhere within the restaurant, even up against walls! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/57290da5755e06f7cb86cd4a5df5bf5ce279cb44.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/0b8a81fc9df80b365b4a4248a77cf9db6dc87b88.png

This change will mean that you’ll be able to accommodate many more customers within a smaller restaurant, and optimise the placement of decorative objects. Table placement and usage will also influence the cleaning mechanic once it's implemented, and we’ll be sharing specifics on that in our next post.

Updates: New restroom models and character animations

With restrooms now arriving at launch our art team has been working on some brand new models and textures to bring these new facilities to life, check out the black marble tiles!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/6587160c2539b662a9d3ff2c6f0e64cdfe15763f.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/1c913adcacd114f46994513c48a36589f6363a70.png

We’ve also started work on new character animations for cleaning actions, disasters, and staff breakdowns.   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/0e656da9de7fa53a9da516002d44ff8763cb506d.gif

Some interesting gestures there...

Well that’s it for today but if you do have any questions please comment on this post or visit our Discord and Twitter. I’ll be back with another update soon!

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster - Progress Update Video #1
notes.content:
Welcome to our very first developer update video!

Following all of your feedback from our Demo in the Steam Next Fest, we’ve added a bunch of new features to the game - and I can’t wait for you to try them all out.

[previewyoutube=n2LSthM2L-0;full][/previewyoutube]


Employee Skill Progression - as employees perform actions, they’ll gain experience in individual skill categories. This will eventually allow them to level up and choose powerful bonus perks. 


New Hiring System - we’ve revised this system so you’ll only receive applications at the start of each day. Which means you’ll have to compromise on who you want to hire!


Dynamic Events - throughout service you may notice someone trying to get your attention. Send an employee over to start up a conversation and choose different dialogue options ranging from friendly to dismissive...


Uniform Templates & Grouping Tool - design your own custom uniforms and assign them to groups. This will allow you to visually organise your team into groups or sections based on their role in the restaurant.


Steam Workshop Integration - this will allow you to upload and share any recipes from your personal cookbook, as well as uniform templates, so anyone can download your creations and use them in their own game!


I want to thank you again for all your feedback so far - we’ve made great progress and we couldn’t do it without your input. Recipe for Disaster will be available to play in Early Access in Q3 this year - so you won’t have to wait long to get stuck into the kitchen and all of our new features!

In the meantime, please feel free to follow us on Twitter and come say hello to the other chefs over in our dedicated Discord.

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster Developer Update #4
notes.content:
Hi everybody, I hope you’re all well! I’ve got some exciting news to share with you today. Having considered all of the excellent feedback that was submitted following our public demo at Steam Next Fest we can now reveal our early access plans and roadmap. I’d also like to talk a little bit about our system for implementing community feedback going forwards and how this will be reflected in the schedule of planned updates. 

Early access roadmap 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/2a788621210e31227db260abd4289edf25b36fc0.png

Content at early access release

Level selector - Each level will come with its own set of objectives tied to a locale. If you played our Steam Next Fest demo you will be familiar with the peaceful small town/rural setting, and we’ve recently been working on the bustling downtown stage. Check out the tenements and urban amenities!   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/da67154df5d6cf4a6b0c4c512f57342bf796a65c.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/d36d6c7f71915126c1754a86859bfb2e23db5776.png

Employee skill progression - Off the back of the demo we found that this was one of the most highly requested features from the community. Staff will now gain experience in specific skill categories as they complete associated tasks. Not only will this experience improve their performance, but it will also allow them to unlock perks which grant additional benefits that help to support the wider team.   

Recruitment changes - Another much requested feature which will add an additional layer of challenge. The recruitment pool is now limited which will mean that when you find yourself short staffed you’ll probably have to compromise on the quality of new recruits. Conversely once your restaurant starts to gain a good reputation, you’ll attract highfliers who come with hefty price tag.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/22eb14069bd0c9ea770cded1575592d0c31cedfc.png

Kitchen and front of house roles - Recipe for Disaster will only get more and more chaotic as we introduce new features during early access, so we thought we’d add a tool early on to help you get organised! We’re currently working on a uniform editor and grouping tool which will allow you to assign staff to particular roles and provide visual cues as to the tasks that they will be performing.    

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/97a4d3e04e42114472d1f37ac9d57d156b919e6f.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/b38383f447a6ee508e84ac4d684963bdb826ec0d.jpg

Localisation - We are just in the process of confirming the final details on this but the game will be available to play in a selection of languages at EA launch. Exact details on which languages will be included will be revealed in the next few weeks.
   
Initial modding support with Workshop - We’re really keen to see what the community can come up with here! A feature that has been requested is the ability to import cookbooks and recipes created by other users, and this is now possible. You’ll also be able to share your custom uniform templates for other players to enjoy.  

To show our progress on these features, we’ll be releasing a few update videos over the coming weeks so you can see for yourselves how they work in practice.

Planned for development and community feedback

Please be aware that this section of the roadmap is a broad overview of our plans leading up to a final, full release and that the precise order of updates is not included here. Rest assured though that we will release detailed information about the first update shortly before early access begins.

Major content updates will be pushed every 4 - 8 weeks, with the exact frequency being determined by the level of community feedback that we receive at certain points on the timeline. As with Rise of Industry we believe that listening to and responding to player’s feedback will be central to development during early access, and you will be able to submit critical feedback and feature requests through an in-game form and via a dedicated channel on our Discord. 

I hope that’s provided some clarity on our EA plans and given you lots to get excited about! As always thanks for stopping by and check back soon for another progress update. 

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster Developer Update #3
notes.content:
Hey everyone, I hope you’re good! I wanted to personally thank those of you that have already taken the time to try out our demo and submit feedback. If you haven’t had a chance to play yet, we are keeping the demo live until Sunday 11th July, so still plenty of time to still get involved. 

With regards to the feedback that we received so far, I thought it would be useful to highlight some of the points raised and share how we will be acting upon them as we continue development.

Demo feedback    

After finishing the demo, we asked players to rate different aspects of the game, and the areas that you felt required the most improvement were:


 Restaurant building options
 Sense of challenge
 Stock management system. 


So this has encouraged us to focus our efforts on improving these aspects first! Alongside the QoL and tutorial feedback (really helpful), we also received the following common suggestions, which I’ll now address:

Recipe editor and menu tools 

“I’d like to customise the appearance of my dishes more” - We can add additional 3D models and improve the usability of the UI on the recipe editor to support this.
 
“It would be great to have a small premade recipe book with suggestions for dishes!” - Recipe for Disaster now supports modding via Steam Workshop, which means that you can share your recipes with others! 


Staff hiring and management systems

“Can staff skill levels be improved over time? How about staff training?” - Staff will level up skills depending on how frequently they perform certain actions, so if a staff member spends a lot of time on the grill they will level up their grill skill.  

“It’s too easy refreshing the staff pool to always get who I want. Could this be a bit more restricted?” - Staff hiring is an incredibly important part of the game. As such the player will only be able to pick from a finite pool at certain points during gameplay which will mean that choices really matter. By EA release we also plan to include one-time applicants who will be exceptional workers, but come with a hefty price tag. 

“It would be helpful to have more visual differentiation between staff depending on their main job e.g. servers and chefs” - We will add roles and uniforms which allow you to visually group staff together.

Pacing

“The gameplay loop gets quite intense! Could we have more unexpected occurrences that break up gameplay?” - We plan to add more social interactions, events, additional weather mechanics, mishaps and disasters to create more variety in the gameplay loop. Some of this will appear in-game during Early Access. 

Restaurant building and customisation tools

“Please can we have MORE placeable objects and customisation options!” - Of course you can! We’ll continue to add new objects to the game including ones that have specific themes to give your restaurant’s more character. 

“It feels like tables are too spaced out, and I’d like to be able to place my tables next to walls” - The plan is to implement tables which can be linked together, so for example, you’ll be able to combine two tables of two, to make one table of four. We’ll also make sure that you can place tables against walls, allowing you to fit more objects within a smaller area.

Sense of challenge

“More variety in goals and milestones would be welcome” - Each level will have its own specific objectives, on top of this we plan to implement a sandbox mode with configurable goals.

“It would be cool to see VIPs or restaurant critics” - Definitely! VIPs and critics appear as an event and will have very high standards! If you manage to impress them they will give you a huge boost in popularity! 

“There needs to be greater clarity on what determines a customer’s review score” - We will continue to work on how reviews are presented in the UI to show exactly what is influencing customer opinion.

Ingredients stock management and ordering system

“The express delivery and keep minimum stock options are confusing. Could this be simplified?” - We’ve streamlined this system by removing the express delivery option, and adding hourly delivery windows. This should make the process of ordering and managing stock feel more intuitive.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/361344283d2a8d196385edee71e94e8e7d28947d.png

“How about additional storage objects that allow you to store specific ingredients, for example a fish tank?” - A great idea, we’re thinking of adding objects such as a lobster tank and herb garden to provide additional storage for new and exclusive ingredients.

Updates: New landscaping objects and improved lighting

Our art department has been working hard on creating new landscaping objects to beautify the exterior of your restaurant and make it more pleasant for customers dining al fresco! 

We also added more realistic grass textures and new specular lighting to really highlight the contrast in light and shadow within the game’s environments.   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/79b5e23916e61b656e1add73d3d748d4b2a766eb.png

That’s all for now but I’ll be back soon with another progress update. Take care until then!

Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster Developer Update #2
notes.content:
Hello, aspiring chefs! Development is currently in high gear but I wanted to take a moment to touch base, start digging into some features, and share progress.  

In today’s post we are going to take our first look at perhaps the most vital component of any successful restaurant: its employees. In Recipe for Disaster you will have full control over who you hire and fire. All aspects of an individual employee, from their appearance to their skills and personality, are procedurally generated which means that every team will be unique.

Employee skills

When deciding who to hire the first thing that you’re going to want to look at are an individual’s skills. All skills range from levels 1 - 5 and, right now, can be broadly broken down into two categories: cooking skills and non-cooking skills (more skills may be added as we continue development).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/6dede115c06ab2f0a0f2b6314f69ddf883b88cb3.png

Cooking skills 

These relate to one of the five main kitchen appliances; the countertop, fryer, grill, oven, and stove. The higher the skill level, the greater the probability of a boost to the food quality of a dish that utilises the associated appliance. Be careful though as conversely, the lower the level, the greater the chance that a dish will receive a negative modifier e.g. Burnt!    

Non-cooking skills 

The charisma skill level affects how successfully an employee is at boosting the mood/attitude of colleagues and customers when things start to go south. The serving skill relates to an employee’s ability to deliver good customer service and directly affects how customers perceive service quality. Carrying determines the likelihood of an employee dropping ingredients and dishes during preparation and service, whilst the cleaning skill affects the efficiency and thoroughness of cleaning actions throughout the restaurant.

Loved and hated skills

On top of all this, every employee will have one loved skill and one hated skill. 

When employees perform actions that utilise a loved or hated skill they will receive either a positive boost or negative hit to their mood/attitude level. This is important because if you don’t look after your employees welfare there will be consequences!

I know I’ve hinted at a number of other mechanics that link up with employee skills, and I’ll be going over all of them in future posts, but hopefully this is enough to get started for now.


Updates: 3D models, appliance lighting FX, and soundtrack preview 

We’ve just started adding 3D models that will appear when employees use appliances. The pans below are linked to the stove specifically but each appliance will have its own set of models. Anyone for surf and turf?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/2ec4f6de37cb32e7f4d4bd20229e7920cec07cbc.png

Speaking of appliances we’re currently working on lighting FX to make the kitchen look and feel really intense. Check out the warm glow of the oven. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/3446cbe7432b3aded5cbb5ed55a0d3ad09ebee67.png

Finally, I think we can all agree that music plays a huge part in defining the atmosphere and mood of a game, so have a listen HERE to a quick preview of one of the ambient tracks that plays during service to get an idea of what we are aiming for...

Thanks for stopping by and feel free to join our Discord and follow us on Twitter, the support is greatly appreciated. We’ll be back with another update soon. 

Alex Mochi
Founder and lead designer - Dapper Penguin Studios

notes.title: Recipe for Disaster Developer Update #1
notes.content:
Hi! Alex here, founder and lead designer for Dapper Penguin Studios. In March we were really stoked to be able to announce our new game Recipe for Disaster and I thought now would be the perfect time to introduce the game personally and answer a few questions that you may have about the project and its ambitions for the future.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/dfe77a2053f3966765999332ca6da648019f6d1b.png


We are keen to keep our community updated on progress throughout development so you can expect regular updates from the team here. Also if you haven’t joined already, please do come and say hi on our Discord and follow us over on Twitter. 

Okay, let's get started!

Q: How did Recipe for Disaster come to light?

Prior to my work as a game designer I actually spent several years working as a waiter and cook. I even went to cooking school, studying 9 hours a day with the plan being to land a job at a Michelin star restaurant. Life didn’t quite work out as intended and I ended up getting into IT and game development, which took me all over to the world and to many well-known companies. After a while I felt I wanted to do things my way and in 2016 I founded Dapper Penguin Studios, releasing our first game Rise of Industry in 2019, shortly followed by its futuristic 2130 DLC. Recipe for Disaster was intended to be a cooldown project following ROI, but has since developed into a much more ambitious title.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/a8d85c1b40658e0d5579d83681dd72464be2a0a9.png


I’m sure a few of you will be able to relate to this, but the years spent working in the food service industry were ‘eye-opening’ to say the least, and it got me thinking about how NPC employees are represented in traditional management and tycoon games. This ended up being the foundation for Recipe for Disaster’s design.  

Q: How are employees handled in Recipe for Disaster?

Have you ever worked in a place where everyone just quietly gets on with their job without any kind of personality, ambition or conflict? Yeah me neither, and yet in almost all tycoon and management games, staff perform their roles with an unnatural, mechanical consistency. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/a6d07ad15cf2ecf0494e31b488aa4c12a7ca4d25.png


We wanted to change that. In Recipe for Disaster you don't really know how your new hires will fit in with the rest of the team, how they'll behave next month or if their personality will change as a result of someone else's actions. The game’s focus is therefore on the social and human side of having a business: customers not always being right, employees fighting, suppliers not delivering what they should've, you know, the day-to-day things that happen in real life.

Q: Will each restaurant have its own personality?

All NPCs will have a great deal of individual personality, with a unique loadout of skills, strengths, weaknesses, ambitions, traits and quirks. Even at this early stage of development it's almost impossible to find two NPCs that are the same!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40139653/bc99f450e1a3e2947e7a78209d39add41145ce19.png


Aside from the staff that you hire, a huge part of making players feel connected to the game world is through restaurant customisation. We currently have a restaurant editor with many placeable objects, textures, walls, floors, and decor. We also spent a lot of time fine-tuning an in-depth recipe editor which allows you to recreate your favourite dishes and learn how recipes work in real life. It’s really fun and intuitive! 

Q: What else do you have planned?

Even with everything that we have done so far we still have a huge amount of work to do! The biggest features that are planned include:


 Multiplayer - Up to 4 player competitive head to head.
 Employee relationships - As time goes by employees will develop affection and distaste for one another.
 Special VIP customers and health inspections - Timed events which will put pressure on the player.
 Roles and uniforms - Clear roles and responsibilities for individual employees.
 Disasters - Appliance breakdowns, staff accidents and mistakes. 
 Modding Support - Players will be able to design their own events, customer types, objects and stages. 


Of course we’ll go into more detail once we are ready to show. 

I hope you’ve enjoyed this short intro to the game. In the coming weeks we’ll be sharing more information about incoming features and progress, but until then thanks for dropping by!


Alex Mochi
Founder & Lead Designer - Dapper Penguin Studios
